question: Why is active listening and counseling so important when nursing patients with reproductive issues?

options.A: To make sure they follow hospital visiting hours
options.B: To diagnose mental health disorders on our own
options.C: To replace the need for any surgery or medicine
options.D: To help them talk through emotional pain and body worries

explanation: Wonderful! Reproductive issues can bring deep worry and sadness. Listening to our patients validates their feelings and supports total healing.

question: What three things make up the surgical fire triangle?

options.A: Heat, light, and pressure
options.B: Ignition source, oxidizer, and fuel
options.C: Anesthetic gas, patient, and surgeon
options.D: Electricity, water, and metal

explanation: Correct! A fire needs a spark (ignition), oxygen (oxidizer), and something to burn (fuel) to start in the theatre.

question: Which bone is located at the very back of a baby's skull?

options.A: The occipital bone
options.B: The frontal bone
options.C: The sphenoid bone
options.D: The temporal bone

explanation: Spot on! The occipital bone sits at the back and forms the lower base and rear part of the skull.

question: A patient asks if boiling drinking water will fully protect their family from schistosomiasis. As a nurse, what is your best reply?

options.A: Yes, but you also need to avoid skin contact with river water during washing or swimming.
options.B: No, boiling water does nothing because the parasites are only caught by eating raw fish.
options.C: No, you must chemically treat the water with chlorine tablets to kill the snail eggs.
options.D: Yes, because the disease is spread exclusively by drinking unboiled water from streams.

explanation: While drinking clean water is always smart, skin contact is the main trap here! Bathing or washing clothes in infested streams is how most people catch it.

question: Which patient position is most commonly used for a routine proctoscopy?

options.A: Left lateral Sims' position
options.B: Prone flat on the abdomen
options.C: Trendelenburg flat position
options.D: Supine with legs in stirrups

explanation: You got it! The left lateral (or Sims') position is the standard, most comfortable posture for a patient during this exam.

question: What major postpartum emergency is an anaemic woman most at risk for?

options.A: Sudden closing of her airway
options.B: Sudden buildup of amniotic fluid
options.C: Hypovolemic shock from normal blood loss
options.D: Temporary leg paralysis

explanation: Since her blood reserves are already low, losing even a standard amount of blood after birth can push her straight into shock.

question: Which of these everyday life stages is a major trigger for cervical ectropion?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Pregnancy
options.D: Menopause

explanation: Pregnancy floods the body with high levels of estrogen, which commonly brings out or worsens cervical ectropion. It's a normal physiological change during this time!

question: Which federal law requires healthcare facilities to inform patients about advance directives upon admission?

options.A: The Patient Self-Determination Act
options.B: The Nursing Practice Act
options.C: The Health Insurance Portability Act
options.D: The Affordable Care Act

explanation: Passed in 1991, the Patient Self-Determination Act ensures that patients are told about their right to make advance directives when entering a healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why should student nurses care about the national reproductive health framework?

options.A: It allows them to practice independently without a supervising physician
options.B: It exempts them from clinical documentation requirements
options.C: It guarantees automatic promotion within the civil service
options.D: It ensures their local community nursing actions match national health goals

explanation: Spot on! Aligning everyday nursing care with national policies helps us all work together effectively to solve health challenges in Nigeria.

question: When does intrapartum transmission of HIV primarily take place?

options.A: Through breast milk during the first week of life
options.B: As the baby passes through the birth canal
options.C: Across the placenta during the first trimester
options.D: Via airborne droplets in the delivery room

explanation: Intrapartum transmission happens when the infant is exposed to infected maternal blood and vaginal fluids during labor and birth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: How can you keep hands clean in a clinic when the running water supply stops?

options.A: Use set-up handwashing stations like Veronica buckets and alcohol rubs
options.B: Wipe hands clean with ordinary office paper towels
options.C: Wear the same pair of examination gloves all day long
options.D: Skip handwashing until municipal water lines are fully restored

explanation: Brilliant! Improvised running-water setups like Veronica buckets and alcohol-based rubs keep patient care safe even when the taps go dry.

question: A cancer patient is exercising. Which sign means you should stop the activity right away?

options.A: A slight increase in heart rate during active movement
options.B: Mild muscle soreness in the legs after walking twenty steps
options.C: Sudden chest pain, severe shortness of breath, and dizziness
options.D: Desire to rest after completing a supervised stretching routine

explanation: Always watch out for red flags! Chest pain, dizziness, and trouble breathing mean the heart or lungs are struggling during exercise.

question: Why does empowering women often lead to smaller, more planned families?

options.A: Employers legally restrict female workers from starting families
options.B: Women lose their biological capacity to conceive after higher education
options.C: Women gain greater decision-making power over their reproductive health
options.D: Government laws force educated women to have fewer children

explanation: Spot on! When women are empowered, they have a stronger voice in deciding family size and birth spacing.

question: What color is the sputum typically seen in a patient with a lung fluke infection?

options.A: Rusty-brown or blood-stained
options.B: Clear and watery
options.C: Bright frothy pink
options.D: Thick yellowish-green

explanation: Spot on! As the parasite cysts break open inside the airways, they release a mix of blood and eggs, giving the sputum a classic rusty look.

question: How should a nurse talk to a patient about their use of local herbal mixtures to ensure safety?

options.A: Ignoring home remedies to focus solely on orthodox hospital drugs
options.B: Telling the patient immediately that all local herbs are dangerous poison
options.C: Reporting the patient to hospital security for using unapproved substances
options.D: Asking calm, non-judgmental questions about all home remedies used

explanation: Wonderful! Being open and non-judgmental builds trust, making patients feel safe to share what they are taking.

question: What is a major sign of a high bowel blockage like a duodenal obstruction?

options.A: Inability to pass flatus
options.B: Bright red rectal bleeding
options.C: Frequent projectile vomiting
options.D: Watery diarrhea with mucus

explanation: Spot on! When the upper digestive tract is blocked, food and fluids have nowhere to go but back up, leading to frequent vomiting of stomach contents.

question: Biological sex is primarily determined by which of the following?

options.A: The cultural expectations placed on a child by family
options.B: How a person presents themselves in the community
options.C: The type of clothing a person chooses to wear
options.D: Anatomical and physiological traits like chromosomes

explanation: Biological sex relates to physical markers such as chromosomes, hormones, and reproductive organs rather than social or cultural factors. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h2)

question: An instructor gives you tips on your sterile technique halfway through your ward posting so you can fix your mistakes. What kind of evaluation is this?

options.A: Affective evaluation
options.B: Norm-referenced evaluation
options.C: Summative evaluation
options.D: Formative evaluation

explanation: That's a formative evaluation! Getting guidance while you are still learning helps you improve on the spot. You're building solid clinical habits.

question: How do school health programs help students do better in their studies?

options.A: By guaranteeing admission to higher education
options.B: By replacing traditional classroom teaching hours
options.C: By eliminating the need for private tutoring
options.D: By reducing absences caused by preventable illnesses

explanation: Spot on! When kids are healthy and miss fewer classes due to preventable sicknesses, they stay on top of their lessons.

question: What is a common cultural view in some Nigerian communities that affects family planning?

options.A: Children born in large numbers are automatically given free education
options.B: Large family sizes are seen as a sign of wealth and prestige
options.C: Small families are forbidden by ancestral spirits
options.D: Contraception is required by traditional law for all couples

explanation: In many cultures, having many children is traditionally viewed as a great blessing and a symbol of high status, which can make people hesitant about birth control.

question: Why is it important to let the nurse share their side of the story during an investigation?

options.A: To ensure fairness and uncover any misunderstood details
options.B: To trick the nurse into admitting a bigger crime
options.C: To let the nurse write the final company policies
options.D: To delay the disciplinary process indefinitely

explanation: Listening to the employee provides a complete picture, ensuring management does not act on incomplete information. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h6)

question: A community nurse is preparing to measure a toddler's MUAC. Where on the arm should the tape be placed to find the correct midpoint?

options.A: At the thickest part of the bicep muscle
options.B: Right below the armpit crease
options.C: Directly over the middle of the forearm
options.D: Between the shoulder tip and the elbow tip

explanation: You've got this! To get an accurate MUAC, always locate the exact midpoint between the shoulder (acromion) and the elbow (olecranon).

question: Why is the nurse often the first person to spot early signs of poor nutrition in a patient?

options.A: Nurses perform the initial admission assessments and spend the most direct time with patients
options.B: Nurses are legally responsible for preparing all hospital meal trays
options.C: Nurses hold advanced degrees in clinical biochemistry and food science
options.D: Nurses alone have the authority to prescribe therapeutic hospital diets

explanation: Spot on! Because you are right there at the bedside doing admissions and checking on patients constantly, you are in the best position to notice changes in their nutrition.

question: How do quality improvement teams use data like fall rates and skin injury reports?

options.A: To hide negative clinical outcomes from state regulatory agencies.
options.B: To track performance trends and guide system-wide safety improvements.
options.C: To find individual nurses to blame whenever an accident happens.
options.D: To determine which residents should be discharged immediately.

explanation: Quality improvement isn't about blaming people—it's about spotting trends so we can make our hospital or facility safer for everyone!

question: Why must petroleum jelly and open flames be strictly avoided around active oxygen delivery equipment?

options.A: Grease stops the oxygen machine from making a buzzing sound
options.B: Oxygen strongly supports and quickens combustion and fire
options.C: Petroleum products block the tiny holes in the nasal cannula
options.D: Flames cause the oxygen tank to instantly fill with water

explanation: Oxygen makes fires burn much hotter and faster, so any spark or flame near an oxygen source creates an extreme fire hazard. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is empowering women through education considered a key objective within population policies?

options.A: It ensures women never participate in agricultural activities.
options.B: It forces families to move permanently to urban centers.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any maternal healthcare clinics.
options.D: It naturally influences family size choices and improves overall health.

explanation: Education is a game-changer! When women are educated, they often choose to marry a bit later, seek out better healthcare, and freely decide on family sizes that work best for them.

question: You see a senior nurse recapping a needle with both hands. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Kindly remind them of the risk and suggest a safer way
options.B: Report them to the police right away
options.C: Ignore it because they have more experience
options.D: Copy them so you can finish your work faster

explanation: Be polite and respectful, but speak up! Friendly peer reminders build a safer, more supportive workplace for everyone.

question: Why does the body rely on both innate and adaptive defenses?

options.A: Innate destroys viruses while adaptive only handles bacterial infections
options.B: Innate immunity creates antibodies while adaptive creates physical barriers
options.C: Adaptive defense works entirely independently of the innate system
options.D: Innate provides immediate defense while adaptive targets specific invaders later

explanation: Spot on! Innate immunity jumps in instantly to buy time, while the adaptive system gears up to launch a precise, targeted attack.

question: What does the skin usually look like right after a long-term cast is removed?

options.A: Bright red, inflamed, and completely covered in blisters
options.B: Dry, scaly, and pale with accumulated dead skin cells
options.C: Deeply tanned from being shielded from outdoor sunlight
options.D: Oily, moist, and smelling strongly of fresh antiseptic lotion

explanation: Because dead skin cells couldn't shed normally while trapped in the cast, the skin looks dry and flaky when the cast finally comes off.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks when assessing a patient's personal host status?

options.A: Screening for underlying chronic illnesses like diabetes
options.B: Inquiring about recent travel history to endemic regions
options.C: Reviewing the patient's personal immunization records
options.D: Analyzing the genetic makeup of the local water supply

explanation: Host assessment is all about the *person* sitting in front of you—their health, vaccines, and history. Water genetics belong to environmental health, not individual patient assessment!

question: At what tier of government is primary health care and public health nursing primarily managed in Nigeria?

options.A: Local government level
options.B: International embassy level
options.C: Global health organization level
options.D: Private corporate level

explanation: Nigeria's primary health care system is decentralized and managed primarily at the local government area level. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which type of dietary fiber is best known for adding bulk to stool and keeping things moving smoothly in the gut?

options.A: Simple fiber
options.B: Glycogen fiber
options.C: Soluble fiber
options.D: Insoluble fiber

explanation: Spot on! Insoluble fiber doesn't break down easily, so it adds bulk and helps prevent constipation.

question: What is the very first step in the community health decision-making process?

options.A: Evaluate the final outcome
options.B: Allocate available funds
options.C: Develop alternative solutions
options.D: Identify the problem

explanation: You cannot solve an issue until you clearly define and recognize what the actual health problem is using data. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to use traditional home remedies like forcing caustic liquids or oils down someone's throat after they swallow a poison?

options.A: Traditional remedies always cure toxic exposures faster than modern hospital drugs.
options.B: Community members refuse to visit hospitals unless accompanied by a nurse.
options.C: Practices like forcing caustic liquids or oils down the throat can worsen tissue injury and cause aspiration.
options.D: Myths prevent patients from paying their hospital bills on time.

explanation: Forcing things down can cause the chemical to burn the throat a second time on the way back up, or slip into the lungs and cause deadly pneumonia. Always educate gently against this!

question: What is the main job of the innermost layer of the gut (the mucosa)?

options.A: Secreting mucus and absorbing nutrients
options.B: Providing a tough outer protective cover
options.C: Supplying blood vessels to the muscle layer
options.D: Pushing food forward through peristalsis

explanation: You got this! The mucosa is the innermost lining of your digestive tract, and its main work is to secrete protective mucus and absorb all the good nutrients from your food.

question: Why is spotting early warning signs so important in a relapse prevention plan?

options.A: It guarantees that the client will never experience symptoms again
options.B: It proves that the client is fully cured of the mental illness
options.C: It allows for early intervention before a full psychotic crisis develops
options.D: It gives the insurance company a reason to stop funding home visits

explanation: Spot on! Catching small changes early—like trouble sleeping or rising anxiety—lets us step in before things turn into an emergency.

question: Why do doctors often order bladder irrigation right after prostate surgery?

options.A: To stretch the bladder muscle back to its normal size
options.B: To prevent dangerous blood clots from blocking urine drainage
options.C: To deliver strong pain medication directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To check if the kidneys are producing enough red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! Surgery areas tend to bleed a bit, and a steady flush stops clots from choking off the catheter.

question: What type of language should a nurse use when documenting physical exam findings?

options.A: Vague and generalized terms like 'fine'
options.B: Subjective opinions about the patient's attitude
options.C: Clear, objective, and descriptive language
options.D: Complex poetic metaphors to describe wounds

explanation: Objective descriptions prevent confusion and provide clear facts for other healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Oh no! A scrub nurse receives a broken suture needle from the surgeon. What should they do first?

options.A: Ask the surgeon to replace the needle holder
options.B: Wait until the end of the operation to mention the break
options.C: Ensure all pieces of the broken needle are accounted for
options.D: Throw the broken pieces into the general waste bin

explanation: You are learning fast! Every single piece of a broken sharp must be found right away so nothing is left inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which medication class is well known for increasing blood sugar levels during therapy?

options.A: Laxatives
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Corticosteroids
options.D: Antihistamines

explanation: Corticosteroids stimulate hepatic glucose production and induce insulin resistance, frequently raising blood sugar levels. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h8)

question: What causes the appearance of the dark vertical line on the abdomen, known as the linea nigra, in pregnant women?

options.A: Stretching of deep muscle fibers beneath the skin surface
options.B: Pooling of deoxygenated blood in superficial abdominal veins
options.C: Increased secretion of melanocyte-stimulating hormone
options.D: Deposition of excess calcium salts in the outer skin layers

explanation: Elevated hormone levels stimulate pigment-producing cells in the skin, leading to darkening in specific areas like the abdomen and face. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h5)

question: What is the basic building block of all living human structures?

options.A: Organs
options.B: Cells
options.C: Tissues
options.D: Systems

explanation: Cells are recognized universally as the fundamental units of structure and function in the human body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h1)

question: When should a nurse evaluate the skin reaction for a tuberculosis skin test?

options.A: 12 to 24 hours
options.B: 7 days
options.C: Immediately after injection
options.D: 48 to 72 hours

explanation: Tuberculosis skin reactions take time to develop, so the immune response is most accurately measured between 48 and 72 hours later. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h5)

question: An AED has just delivered a shock to a cardiac arrest patient. What should you do next?

options.A: Turn off the AED and wait for the doctor
options.B: Immediately resume chest compressions
options.C: Check for a carotid pulse for 30 seconds
options.D: Give two rescue breaths without compressions

explanation: Don't wait! Right after a shock is delivered, jump straight back into CPR starting with chest compressions.

question: What is the main medical use for mannitol, a special osmotic diuretic?

options.A: Treating chronic leg swelling from varicose veins
options.B: Lowering high pressure inside the brain
options.C: Lowering blood sugar in diabetic patients
options.D: Managing everyday high blood pressure

explanation: Mannitol acts like a strong magnet, pulling fluid out of swollen brain tissues and into the blood vessels to quickly relieve pressure.

question: Why do some heart tumours cause symptoms that look just like regular heart failure?

options.A: The tumour causes the coronary arteries to permanently spasm
options.B: The tumour takes up space in the heart chambers and reduces the amount of blood pumped out
options.C: Cardiac tumours completely stop the production of red blood cells
options.D: Cardiac tumours directly destroy the brain's ability to regulate heart rate

explanation: When an extra mass takes up room inside the heart, the chambers can't hold or push out enough blood. This causes fluid to back up, mimicking heart failure. Great job thinking it through!

question: Which neurotransmitter is most directly linked to the brain's reward pathway and addiction?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Histamine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Dopamine is the primary chemical messenger responsible for reinforcing rewarding experiences in the brain's reward center. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why do nurses refer to pain as the 'fifth vital sign'?

options.A: It directly calculates the exact heart rate of the patient.
options.B: It can be measured using an automated cuff machine.
options.C: It must be checked and recorded alongside standard vital signs.
options.D: It is only relevant during surgical procedures.

explanation: Calling pain the fifth vital sign reminds us to assess and document it just as regularly as temperature or blood pressure. Great job keeping your clinical habits sharp!

question: Why is giving incorrect drug information a serious ethical and legal mistake for a nurse?

options.A: It prevents the pharmaceutical company from selling more medications
options.B: It takes too much time away from routine ward cleaning duties
options.C: It can directly harm the patient and violates the professional duty of care
options.D: It lowers the overall financial revenue of the hospital pharmacy

explanation: You got it! Our primary duty is to protect our patients from harm, which means we must always provide accurate drug guidance.

question: Why is maintaining good hydration crucial for a patient with sickle cell disease?

options.A: It speeds up the breakdown of old iron deposits in the liver
options.B: It stops the bone marrow from producing abnormal platelets
options.C: It increases the total number of white blood cells in circulation
options.D: It keeps blood thin and prevents red blood cells from sickling

explanation: Dehydration concentrates the blood and causes red blood cells to warp and block vessels, so fluids help prevent painful crises. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is a primary health care nurse in a great position to monitor community diseases?

options.A: They possess the authority to declare national state emergencies
options.B: They interact directly with local patients and see early signs of illness
options.C: They work exclusively inside high-tech research laboratories abroad
options.D: They are responsible for importing vaccines from international suppliers

explanation: Because community nurses talk to patients every single day, they are usually the very first to notice when something unusual is going on.

question: Why is losing a pulse considered a very late and dangerous sign of compartment syndrome?

options.A: Arteries have thick walls and are the last vessels to collapse under pressure.
options.B: Pulse checks are unreliable unless done with a special electronic machine.
options.C: Blood flow actually increases in the early stages of compartment pressure.
options.D: Nerves stop working before blood vessels even begin to narrow.

explanation: Major arteries are tough and hold out the longest. Nerves and tiny capillaries get crushed and starved of oxygen way before the main pulse disappears.

question: What is the preferred way to feed a patient with a major burn injury?

options.A: Total parenteral nutrition through a central line
options.B: Enteral nutrition via feeding tube
options.C: Strict oral diet supplemented only by clear fluids
options.D: Intravenous amino acid infusions without lipids

explanation: Feed the gut if it works! Early tube feeding keeps the stomach lining strong, stops bacteria from leaking, and fuels their massive healing needs.

question: Why is it dangerous to start a health program without doing a situation analysis first?

options.A: Community members will refuse to ever speak to healthcare workers
options.B: The government will refuse to disburse salaries to the nursing staff
options.C: Local pharmacy shops will immediately report the clinic to the police
options.D: The program might target problems the community does not consider important

explanation: Skipping situation analysis often leads to wasted resources because interventions fail to address the actual priorities of the local population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h1)

question: How does regular physical activity benefit a patient with Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: It helps body cells respond better to available insulin
options.B: It allows the patient to eat unlimited amounts of sugar
options.C: It permanently repairs destroyed cells inside the pancreas
options.D: It replaces the daily need for checking blood sugar levels

explanation: Exercise makes muscle and tissue cells more sensitive to insulin, allowing glucose to move out of the blood and into cells more easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: What do we call the deep worry families feel about potentially losing a loved one with HIV?

options.A: Chronic denial syndrome
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Situational psychosis
options.D: Secondary infection

explanation: Well done! Anticipatory grief happens when families start grieving and worrying about future loss long before any severe physical decline occurs.

question: Which class of blood pressure medication works primarily by helping the kidneys remove excess water and sodium from the body?

options.A: Diuretics
options.B: Statins
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Beta-blockers

explanation: Diuretics, or water pills, prompt the kidneys to excrete sodium and water, reducing overall blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h5)

question: What makes needle-stick injuries so scary for us on the clinical floor?

options.A: They automatically disqualify a nurse from clinical duty
options.B: They cause immediate systemic allergic reactions
options.C: They can transmit serious bloodborne pathogens easily
options.D: They always lead to permanent nerve damage in the hand

explanation: Exactly. A used needle carries patient blood straight into your bloodstream, which is a major risk for infections. Always handle sharps with care!

question: What is a major long-term health complication frequently managed by nurses in patients who have undergone child marriage and early pregnancy?

options.A: Accelerated bone mineralization and high density
options.B: Permanent blindness caused by vitamin deficiency
options.C: Obstetric fistula and severe pelvic floor damage
options.D: Chronic respiratory infections from cold weather

explanation: Underdeveloped pelvises in young mothers often lead to obstructed labor, resulting in severe complications like obstetric fistula. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h6)

question: Where is the classic landmark for placing an intracardiac injection on the chest?

options.A: Second intercostal space on the right mid-clavicular line
options.B: Third intercostal space directly over the sternum
options.C: Fourth intercostal space just to the left of the sternum
options.D: Fifth intercostal space at the mid-axillary line

explanation: Spotting the right anatomical landmarks is a key nursing skill! This specific spot lets a needle reach the left ventricle while keeping surrounding chest structures safe.

question: As a caring nurse, why should you check in on the emotional wellbeing of a patient with endometriosis?

options.A: Chronic pain and potential fertility challenges can cause significant emotional distress
options.B: Hormonal medications prevent patients from feeling any physical pain
options.C: Mental health counseling can cure the physical growth of endometrial tissue
options.D: Anxiety and depression are the direct physical causes of retrograde menstruation

explanation: Living day in and day out with stubborn pain and worries about having kids can take a heavy emotional toll. Holistic nursing means supporting her mind too!

question: Why is keeping the cuticle intact so important for your patient?

options.A: It gives the nail plate its hard texture
options.B: It controls how fast the nail grows daily
options.C: It supplies the blood flow to the nail bed
options.D: It acts as a seal against bacteria and moisture

explanation: You've got this! Think of the cuticle as a natural bodyguard. It seals out water and germs so they don't slip under the skin and cause infection.

question: Why do patients who recover from a severe kidney injury need long-term blood pressure checks?

options.A: Kidney damage can disrupt blood flow regulation and trigger chronic hypertension.
options.B: Blood pressure medication prevents the formation of scar tissue in the ureter.
options.C: High blood pressure is the primary cause of external genital trauma.
options.D: Kidney injuries always cause permanent low blood pressure due to fluid loss.

explanation: Our kidneys help control our blood pressure. If scarring messes up their hormone signals, it can lead to long-term high blood pressure down the road.

question: Which intervention directly supports the occupational health of school teachers?

options.A: Requiring teachers to grade papers overnight without rest
options.B: Reducing their salaries to encourage financial discipline
options.C: Abolishing all staff lounge and rest facilities
options.D: Providing ergonomic seating and stress management workshops

explanation: Ergonomics and mental health support protect teachers from physical strain and burnout associated with their jobs. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient shows signs of pain while their arm is being moved?

options.A: Continue moving faster to get past the painful spot
options.B: Ask a relative to hold the arm down so you can finish
options.C: Stop the exercise right away and check the joint
options.D: Ignore it because passive exercise always hurts

explanation: Pain is your stop sign! It tells you something is being over-stretched or injured. Always pause and assess.

question: Which clinical sign will immediately make a doctor or nurse think of ordering a liver function panel?

options.A: Frequent coughing
options.B: Painful urination
options.C: Jaundice
options.D: Swollen ankles from heart failure

explanation: Spot on! That yellowing of the eyes and skin (jaundice) tells us bilirubin isn't clearing properly, making LFTs a top priority.

question: What is the main goal of preventive healthcare services in the community?

options.A: To cure advanced stages of chronic organ failure
options.B: To stop diseases from occurring in the first place
options.C: To manage emergency surgical trauma in hospitals
options.D: To replace the need for community health education

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept disease processes before they start through immunizations, hygiene, and safe water practices. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h3)

question: Which group of nutrients does the body need in large amounts?

options.A: Macronutrients
options.B: Micronutrients
options.C: Trace elements
options.D: Antioxidants

explanation: Macro means large! Macronutrients like carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need in heavy quantities every day.

question: How does the body primarily generate heat when exposed to cold environments?

options.A: By increasing sweat production
options.B: Through muscle activity and shivering
options.C: Through rapid blood vessel expansion
options.D: By decreasing cellular metabolism
