question: Why do advanced tumors often become resistant to medical treatments like chemotherapy?

options.A: The body's immune system destroys the medication before it reaches the tumor
options.B: Chemotherapy drugs turn normal cells into malignant cancer cells
options.C: Genetic diversity creates varied cell populations with different drug resistance traits
options.D: Tumor cells develop a protective bone shell that blocks all medications

explanation: As mutations accumulate, cancer cells become diverse; while some cells die from treatment, resistant clones survive and multiply. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a major risk for family members who care for a loved one long-term without a break?

options.A: Sudden medical immunity
options.B: Instant financial wealth
options.C: Caregiver burnout
options.D: Complete loss of empathy

explanation: Looking after someone takes a massive physical and emotional toll. Always remember to check on the caregivers too—they need support to stay strong!

question: What vital sign must you watch most carefully after giving an IV opioid?

options.A: Oxygen saturation only
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Capillary refill
options.D: Body temperature

explanation: Safety first! Opioids can slow down the brain's breathing center, making your respiratory check the most important assessment in the room.

question: Why is teaching patients how to read food labels so important on a low-fat diet?

options.A: Processed foods often contain hidden fats that are not obvious by appearance.
options.B: Labels help the patient calculate the exact cost of groceries.
options.C: Reading labels is a legal requirement for hospital discharge.
options.D: Nutrition labels tell the patient exactly when to take their medications.

explanation: Many packaged snacks hide extra fats where you least expect them. Reading labels helps patients spot those sneaky lipids!

question: Which of the following is NOT a good characteristic of effective instructional materials?

options.A: Relevance to the topic
options.B: Scientific accuracy
options.C: Clarity and simplicity
options.D: Outdated clinical practices

explanation: Instructional materials must always contain current, accurate information; outdated practices can compromise patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h4)

question: What physical sign on a head bandage might make you suspect a leak of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

options.A: A foul-smelling green discharge with pus
options.B: Complete dryness with no visible fluid stains
options.C: Bright red blood soaking through the entire bandage
options.D: A clear yellow halo surrounding a spot of blood

explanation: CSF mixed with blood is clever—it separates on dressings, forming that distinct watery ring or halo right around the blood spot!

question: Which acronym represents the four main stages of pharmacokinetics?

options.A: ABCS
options.B: DOME
options.C: FAST
options.D: ADME

explanation: ADME is your best friend here! It stands for Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. Memorize this, and pharmacology topics become much easier.

question: What vital sign must a nurse always check before a client starts taking combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Oxygen saturation
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Temperature
options.D: Blood pressure

explanation: Always check the BP! Estrogen can push blood pressure up, so we need a safe baseline reading before handing out that first prescription.

question: What is a key principle of modern reproductive rights?

options.A: The right to decide freely the number and spacing of children
options.B: The guarantee of automatic financial support for large families
options.C: The right to free private healthcare delivery anywhere in the world
options.D: The legal obligation to have at least two children per family

explanation: Spot on! Modern rights put the power back in the individual's hands to choose if, when, and how many children they want to have.

question: By about what percentage does plasma volume increase during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: 10 percent
options.B: 50 percent
options.C: 5 percent
options.D: 100 percent

explanation: Amazing! By the third trimester, a pregnant woman's plasma volume shoots up by nearly 50% to nourish the baby and placenta. The female body is truly incredible!

question: What do we mean by 'molecular mimicry' in autoimmune conditions?

options.A: A pathogen shares protein structures with body tissue, confusing the immune system
options.B: Antibodies completely change their shape to match a virus
options.C: Immune cells hide inside healthy organs to escape detection
options.D: Healthy cells pretend to be foreign invaders to trick white blood cells

explanation: Sometimes a germ looks very similar to our own body tissue. When the immune system fights the germ, it accidentally attacks the body tissue too because they look like twins!

question: A patient comes back three days after an injection with a hot, swollen, throbbing lump at the site. What is this most likely?

options.A: A localized muscle abscess
options.B: Systemic blood poisoning
options.C: Chronic hepatitis C infection
options.D: An acute HIV seroconversion illness

explanation: That classic combo of throbbing pain, heat, swelling, and a lump usually points to a bacterial abscess from an unsterile injection that may need draining.

question: Why do vulnerable or socially excluded patients often delay going to the hospital when sick?

options.A: They fear mistreatment, discrimination, or face overwhelming financial and social barriers
options.B: Government policies legally forbid them from entering primary health centers
options.C: They lack any physical symptoms of illness until disease is terminal
options.D: They prefer traditional remedies exclusively over modern clinical treatments

explanation: You got it! Past bad experiences, worries about being judged, or not having enough money often stop people from seeking early help.

question: What emotional change do we often see in patients with Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Extreme violent outbursts toward staff members
options.B: Apathy and lack of emotional spontaneity
options.C: Constant hyperactivity and pacing the hallways
options.D: Hyper-fixation on learning new complex hobbies

explanation: Patients often seem very indifferent, flat, or lacking in energy and initiative. It's part of how the brain injury affects their drive.

question: Why must nurses take a proactive approach rather than waiting for problems to fix themselves?

options.A: Doctors rarely check on patients unless a nurse calls first
options.B: Small clinical issues can rapidly turn into major emergencies
options.C: Proactive nurses are excused from doing routine bedside care
options.D: Hospital policies require nurses to document every minor event

explanation: Acting early prevents minor changes in a patient's condition from worsening into critical crises. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which sign indicates that a patient is developing contrast-induced nephropathy days after an IVP?

options.A: A temporary metallic taste in the mouth
options.B: A sudden rash appearing on the chest
options.C: A delayed rise in serum creatinine levels
options.D: A mild episode of dizziness right after standing

explanation: Kidney injury from contrast dye typically shows up as an abnormal elevation in blood creatinine levels within two days of the test. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is the nursing term for pain or burning when a patient passes urine?

options.A: Proteinuria
options.B: Hematuria
options.C: Dysuria
options.D: Oliguria

explanation: Dysuria is a classic clinical term worth memorizing. 'Dys-' means painful or difficult, and '-uria' refers to urine!

question: Why would community health workers use megaphones in a local market before an immunization drive?

options.A: To record the vital signs of market traders during trading hours
options.B: To diagnose patients with respiratory infections from a distance
options.C: To replace traditional printed posters in the health clinic
options.D: To quickly alert and inform large crowds gathered in a public space

explanation: Megaphones are loud and handy for grabbing attention in busy public spots like markets to announce urgent health events.

question: Which workplace strategy best helps nurses cope with moral distress during end-of-life care?

options.A: Ignoring difficult ethical situations to focus only on physical tasks
options.B: Avoiding all discussions with dying patients and their families
options.C: Participating in regular clinical debriefings and ethics rounds
options.D: Accepting every medical order without questioning its futility

explanation: Talking it out helps! Team debriefings and ethics meetings give nurses a safe space to share their feelings, process tough cases, and find support.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective clinical problem solving?

options.A: Fatigue and physical burnout
options.B: Heavy workloads and rushed decisions
options.C: Adequate staffing and clear communication
options.D: Fear of making mistakes and facing blame

explanation: Adequate staffing and clear communication help problem solving rather than acting as a barrier. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the golden rule of nursing documentation when it comes to legal protection?

options.A: If it was not charted, it was not done
options.B: Only write down abnormal patient vitals
options.C: Always erase mistakes with correction fluid
options.D: Chart at the end of the week from memory

explanation: In the eyes of the law, if you didn't write it down in the chart, it never happened. Document everything you do!

question: Why do we need a team of different professionals in palliative care?

options.A: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members per patient.
options.B: No single profession can address all physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.
options.C: Nurses only handle administrative paperwork in palliative settings.
options.D: Doctors are not allowed to talk to family members directly.

explanation: No single person knows it all! Caring for someone with a serious illness takes doctors, nurses, social workers, and spiritual leaders all working hand-in-hand to cover every angle.

question: Why must nurses check for other physical symptoms alongside pain during a palliative assessment?

options.A: Multiple symptoms interact and can make each other worse, like breathlessness causing panic
options.B: Non-pain symptoms are usually much more dangerous than actual physical pain
options.C: Insurance companies only pay for care if three symptoms are treated at once
options.D: Doctors only look at pain scores and ignore all other bodily complaints

explanation: Symptoms don't happen in isolation. Struggling to breathe can trigger panic, so we need to look at the whole picture!

question: Why do nurses join trade unions and professional associations?

options.A: To replace hospital managers and run the finance department
options.B: To diagnose patients without consulting medical doctors
options.C: To collectively advocate for better working conditions and pay
options.D: To bypass the need for government health laws completely

explanation: Unions give workers collective bargaining power to demand fair wages, safety gear, and reasonable hours. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h6)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Filtering waste and storing urine
options.B: Producing red blood cells and digesting fats
options.C: Producing gametes and secreting sex hormones
options.D: Manufacturing mucus and housing fetal tissue

explanation: The ovaries create egg cells and release hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the first critical step a nurse must take when beginning a clinical assessment with an adolescent and their family?

options.A: Ban all family members from the hospital floor for the duration of the stay.
options.B: Prescribe routine vitamins without consulting the parents or the patient.
options.C: Explain confidentiality limits and conduct part of the interview with the teen alone.
options.D: Ask the teenager to sign a binding financial contract for their medical bills.

explanation: Private interview time allows teenagers to speak freely about sensitive topics, which improves assessment accuracy. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h7)

question: What is the normal age range for the closure of the larger anterior fontanelle?

options.A: 1 to 3 months
options.B: 6 to 8 weeks
options.C: 9 to 18 months
options.D: 24 to 36 months

explanation: Spot on! The big front soft spot takes its time and usually closes between 9 and 18 months of age.

question: What is the main danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Provoking rebound status epilepticus
options.B: Experiencing immediate total amnesia
options.C: Developing chronic high blood pressure
options.D: Causing permanent liver failure

explanation: Abruptly stopping these meds can shock the brain chemistry and trigger severe, continuous seizures. Patient education on compliance is key!

question: What term describes the first menstrual period in adolescent females?

options.A: Menarche
options.B: Menopause
options.C: Thelarche
options.D: Ovulation

explanation: Menarche is the medical term for a young woman's very first menstrual bleeding, marking a key milestone in female physical maturation. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h2)

question: A nurse reviews attendance records and participant feedback after a nutrition workshop. What phase of the nursing process for community programs does this represent?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Assessment
options.D: Diagnosis

explanation: Reviewing records and gathering feedback after a program is finished is part of evaluating its success. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the main difference between passive and active transport?

options.A: Passive transport requires carrier proteins, while active transport does not
options.B: Active transport moves water, while passive transport moves solid particles
options.C: Active transport requires cellular energy, while passive transport does not
options.D: Passive transport only occurs in plant cells, while active transport occurs in animals

explanation: The defining difference is energy use; active transport consumes ATP to push substances against their natural gradient, whereas passive transport uses existing kinetic energy. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main goal of diet therapy in patient care?

options.A: Modifying regular food intake to meet specific health needs
options.B: Reducing hospital kitchen operational costs
options.C: Ensuring every patient eats the exact same meal
options.D: Replacing all forms of medical drug treatment

explanation: You've got this! Diet therapy is simply tailoring a patient's nutrition to help them heal, manage an illness, or balance their body's needs.

question: How deep should the blade go when performing a standard skin snip?

options.A: Superficially into the dermis without deep cutting
options.B: Strictly through the dead outer stratum corneum layer
options.C: Deep into the subcutaneous fat layer for fat cells
options.D: Through the entire muscle layer down to the bone

explanation: You got it! Since the little parasites hang out in the upper skin layers (dermis), we only need a very shallow snip.

question: What does the popular '60/60 rule' recommend when using earphones or headphones?

options.A: Listening at no more than sixty percent volume for sixty minutes daily
options.B: Taking a sixty-minute break after every sixty steps taken
options.C: Keeping the device sixty inches away from the ears at all times
options.D: Using headphones for no more than sixty hours a week

explanation: The 60/60 rule is an easy trick to protect your ears from loud music damage. Try keeping your volume at 60% or lower for no more than 60 minutes a day!

question: What is the main goal of a clinically useful research problem?

options.A: Nursing care and patient health outcomes
options.B: The speed of administrative paperwork
options.C: The personal salary of the lead researcher
options.D: The architectural design of the hospital

explanation: At the end of the day, nursing research is all about making patient care safer and helping people recover better. That's why we do it!

question: What is the most common cause of blunt upper airway trauma in adults?

options.A: Sudden throat infections
options.B: Spontaneous tissue tears
options.C: Motor vehicle collisions
options.D: Severe allergic reactions

explanation: Spot on! Direct impacts from steering wheels or dashboards during car crashes frequently compress neck structures against the spine.

question: Which nerve is most vulnerable to being stretched or compressed during a tough vaginal delivery?

options.A: Sciatic nerve
options.B: Pudendal nerve
options.C: Femoral nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: You're learning fast! The pudendal nerve runs right through the birth canal area, making it easy to stretch or compress during labor.

question: What is the normal healthy pH range for human blood?
explanation: Keep this number in your pocket—a blood pH of 7.35 to 7.45 is a vital sign range that the lungs and kidneys work hard to maintain every single day.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when estimating injection commodity needs?

options.A: Performing regular physical inventory audits on the ward
options.B: Ignoring existing stock levels currently sitting in the storeroom
options.C: Collaborating closely with pharmacy and supply chain personnel
options.D: Reviewing past consumption reports from previous months

explanation: Always subtract what is already in stock from your calculated requirement so you do not accidentally over-order. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a steady and uninterrupted supply of essential medicines
options.B: To provide free medical treatments to all vulnerable populations
options.C: To pay the monthly salaries of clinical and administrative staff
options.D: To generate excess profit for hospital infrastructure development

explanation: Spot on! The DRF is like a rolling fund. Money from drug sales goes right back into buying more drugs so the pharmacy never runs empty.

question: Which injection is routinely given to newborns to prevent bleeding?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Great job! Babies are born with low vitamin K levels, so this shot protects them from bleeding problems.

question: Why is data encryption so important for health wearable devices?

options.A: To increase the physical durability of the wristband strap
options.B: To protect sensitive patient health records from unauthorized interception
options.C: To ensure the step counter measures distance more accurately
options.D: To make the device battery last much longer during daily use

explanation: Encryption scrambles personal health details so hackers can't read or steal confidential patient information.

question: You need to give a routine vaccine to a healthy 12-month-old baby. Which injection site is best?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Ventrogluteal
options.C: Vastus lateralis
options.D: Deltoid

explanation: Spot on! The vastus lateralis (thigh muscle) is nice and plump in little infants, making it the go-to, safe spot for routine baby immunizations.

question: Why is it usually a bad idea to write a research question that can only be answered with a simple 'yes' or 'no'?

options.A: It usually lacks the depth needed to explore complex clinical phenomena
options.B: Ethical boards reject all yes-no questions automatically
options.C: Patients refuse to answer questions with two options
options.D: It is mathematically impossible to analyze yes-no data

explanation: Healthcare is complex! Simple yes/no questions often miss the rich details and depth needed to truly understand patient care.

question: What is a big plus of using a flexible fiberoptic scope instead of a rigid one in the clinic?

options.A: The patient can remain awake and talk while vocal cord movement is assessed.
options.B: It completely eliminates any risk of a patient gagging during the test.
options.C: It provides a wider surgical field for removing large vocal cord tumors.
options.D: It requires full general anesthesia to relax the throat muscles completely.

explanation: Exactly! Because the patient is awake, doctors can actually watch how the vocal cords move when they talk or breathe.

question: Why are pregnant women more likely to get hemorrhoids?

options.A: Loss of sphincter control caused by high estrogen
options.B: Eating too much refined sugar and processed foods
options.C: Increased pelvic venous pressure and straining from constipation
options.D: Direct infection of the rectal mucosa by bacteria

explanation: It's a double whammy: the heavy uterus slows down blood flow from the lower body, and pushing hard due to constipation makes those sensitive veins swell up.

question: What is a major advantage of direct-acting relaxants like mebeverine over anticholinergics?

options.A: They can only be given safely through an intravenous drip
options.B: They work within seconds of entering the bloodstream
options.C: They lack widespread anticholinergic side effects like dry mouth
options.D: They cure the underlying cause of irritable bowel syndrome permanently

explanation: Because they target the gut muscles locally, patients get cramp relief without feeling like their mouth is full of cotton wool!

question: Which test is most commonly used to check for structural causes of secondary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Brain CT scan
options.B: Pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Chest X-ray
options.D: Bone density scan

explanation: Correct! An ultrasound is safe, non-invasive, and great for taking a look at the uterus and ovaries.

question: What is a major community-wide effect when a clinic suffers an outbreak of healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Loss of public trust in the healthcare system
options.B: Lower costs for public health insurance programs
options.C: An immediate surplus of available hospital beds
options.D: Increased willingness of patients to receive injections

explanation: Exactly. When a clinic spreads disease instead of healing, people lose faith and may stop seeking care when they truly need it. Safe nursing builds community trust! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h5)

question: A patient complains of a burning pain in a leg that was surgically removed last week. How should you, as the nurse, respond?

options.A: Acknowledge the pain as real neuropathic discomfort and report it for treatment.
options.B: Tell the patient this feeling is temporary and will vanish within a few hours.
options.C: Suggest that the patient is imagining things because of anxiety over surgery.
options.D: Gently remind the patient that the leg is gone so the pain cannot actually exist.

explanation: Phantom pain is very real! It comes from the cut nerve endings trying to heal, so always validate your patient and get them the relief they need.

question: What is the primary goal of discipline in nursing management?

options.A: To reduce the number of staff on duty
options.B: To correct behavior and protect patients
options.C: To enforce strict administrative control
options.D: To punish nurses who make mistakes

explanation: Management discipline aims to guide staff toward safe practices rather than simply punish them. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of putting a footboard on an immobile patient's bed?

options.A: To relieve pressure on the heels and prevent heel ulcers
options.B: To prevent foot drop by keeping ankles at a ninety-degree angle
options.C: To provide a surface for active leg strengthening exercises
options.D: To stop the patient from sliding down toward the foot of the bed

explanation: A footboard keeps the foot upright at a nice 90-degree angle, stopping the calf muscles from tightening up into foot drop.

question: What is the main benefit of using the teach-back method with a patient?

options.A: It tests the patient's long-term memory from their childhood.
options.B: It replaces the need for any written discharge paperwork.
options.C: It proves to the doctor that the nurse did their job correctly.
options.D: It checks whether the patient truly understood the care instructions.

explanation: You got it! Asking them to explain things back in their own words is the best way to catch any misunderstandings before they go home.

question: In the late stages of CJD, what does the term 'akinetic mutism' mean?

options.A: The patient is completely immobile and unresponsive.
options.B: The patient experiences sudden episodes of paralysis.
options.C: The patient has lost the ability to digest solid food.
options.D: The patient is restless and shouts continuously.

explanation: Correct! Akinetic mutism means the patient can no longer move or speak, remaining entirely quiet and unresponsive to their environment.

question: Which main chemical in tobacco makes it so addictive?

options.A: Ammonia
options.B: Tar
options.C: Carbon monoxide
options.D: Nicotine

explanation: Nicotine is the addictive substance in tobacco that hooks the brain and drives the urge to keep smoking. You've got this!

question: What happens when an osteoblast gets completely trapped inside the hard bone it built?

options.A: It divides rapidly to form new osteons
options.B: It transforms back into a stem cell
options.C: It dissolves into the central canal
options.D: It turns into a mature osteocyte

explanation: Spot on! Once it's completely surrounded by the hard matrix, the builder cell settles down into a maintenance worker known as an osteocyte.

question: How do emergency contraceptive pills work after unprotected sex?

options.A: By thickening the uterine wall to trap the fertilized egg inside
options.B: By delaying or preventing the release of an egg from the ovary
options.C: By permanently destroying all active sperm inside the fallopian tubes
options.D: By causing an immediate surgical termination of an implanted embryo

explanation: Emergency contraceptives act like a pause button on ovulation. They push back the release of the egg so the sperm simply die out waiting. Simple and effective!

question: How long should patients wait at the clinic after getting an immunization?

options.A: At least 15 minutes
options.B: Exactly two hours
options.C: Until the end of the market day
options.D: No waiting time is required

explanation: That 15-minute window is a crucial safety check just in case a rare allergic reaction pops up right away.

question: How long does the postpartum puerperium period typically last?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: You've got this! The puerperium lasts for about six weeks after childbirth. This is the special time the mother's body needs for her reproductive organs to gently return to their normal, non-pregnant state.

question: Your patient with diabetes just took rapid-acting insulin. When is it most critical to make sure they have food?

options.A: Whenever the laboratory technician draws a blood sample
options.B: Only when the patient reports feeling extremely thirsty
options.C: At the time of peak insulin action to prevent hypoglycemia
options.D: Exactly six hours before the insulin injection is given

explanation: Well done! Rapid-acting insulin drops blood sugar fast. Food needs to hit their system right when the insulin peaks to stop blood sugar from crashing too low.

question: What happens to the baby's blood pressure right after the umbilical cord is clamped?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged
options.B: It drops down to zero
options.C: It fluctuates wildly every second
options.D: It increases significantly

explanation: You're doing awesome! Cutting the cord removes the low-resistance placenta, which causes an immediate rise in the baby's blood pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)

question: A teenager avoids emergency contraception because she believes it causes permanent infertility. What type of barrier is this?

options.A: Economic restriction
options.B: Legal impediment
options.C: Psychosocial misconception
options.D: Physical limitation

explanation: Myths and false beliefs about side effects are psychological barriers rooted in misinformation. Gentle education goes a long way here.

question: In the FAST stroke assessment tool, what does the letter 'T' stand for?

options.A: Temperature of the patient's skin
options.B: Tremors in the fingers and hands
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Time to call emergency services

explanation: Time is brain! The 'T' reminds us to call for emergency help immediately when stroke signs appear, because quick action saves brain tissue.

question: What is the main goal of the 'sensitivity' part of a urine culture and sensitivity (C&S) test?

options.A: To determine which antibiotics will kill the specific bacteria
options.B: To measure the exact volume of urine produced in 24 hours
options.C: To calculate the patient's specific gravity and hydration status
options.D: To check if red blood cells are fragile under chemical stress

explanation: The sensitivity test is like a test-run for medicines! It shows us which exact antibiotic will successfully knock out the patient's specific infection.

question: What is the main way condoms stop pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus permanently
options.B: By stopping ovulation in the ovaries
options.C: By trapping semen to keep sperm out of the uterus
options.D: By killing sperm cells inside the testes

explanation: Exactly right! Condoms act as a physical shield that catches semen so the sperm cannot swim up into the reproductive tract.

question: Why is keeping a close eye on vital signs so crucial when a patient is going through alcohol or sedative withdrawal?

options.A: It helps prove to the patient that they have an active drug problem
options.B: It replaces the need to take blood samples for kidney function tests
options.C: Withdrawal from these substances can cause dangerous and life-threatening physical instability
options.D: Vital signs remain completely normal throughout the entire detox process

explanation: Spot on! Unlike some other substances, alcohol and sedative withdrawal can trigger severe seizures and drastic blood pressure changes. Close monitoring keeps the patient safe.

question: Which of these is NOT a good step when setting up a clean workspace on a household table?

options.A: Washing your hands thoroughly before touching any supplies
options.B: Using a clean disposable barrier like a paper towel as your work surface
options.C: Keeping clean supplies separate from used or dirty items
options.D: Spraying the table with a standard household bleach solution right before laying down sterile instruments

explanation: Spray bottles and wet chemicals right next to open supplies can easily contaminate your clean field. Using a dry paper towel barrier is much safer!

question: What is the normal, healthy pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Blood pH is tightly guarded between 7.35 and 7.45. Even a tiny shift outside this window can make a patient very sick, so the body works hard to protect it.

question: When a patient has a blood disorder, why must you check multiple body systems instead of just one area?

options.A: Haematological disorders only affect the skin and the muscles
options.B: Blood circulates throughout the entire body and impacts every organ
options.C: Blood cell counts change completely every single hour
options.D: Hospital protocols require checking every organ for all patients

explanation: Remember, blood travels everywhere! Because it touches every part of the body, a blood problem can show up as symptoms in different organs.

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear that an IUD will cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Tell the client that her fears are irrational and insist she accepts the device anyway
options.B: Provide calm, evidence-based education explaining that fertility returns immediately upon IUD removal
options.C: Agree that permanent damage is common and suggest she avoids all birth control
options.D: Ignore the comment and document that the client refused all medical advice

explanation: Respectful nursing care involves correcting myths gently with factual information while supporting the client's ultimate autonomy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: Why does a narrowed coronary artery cause chest pain during physical exertion?

options.A: The heart muscle receives less oxygen than it needs for extra work
options.B: Blood rushes too fast through the narrow tube and bursts small vessels
options.C: The heart valves stop opening completely due to pressure changes
options.D: The lungs cannot pump enough air to match the heart rate

explanation: When the body works harder, the heart needs more oxygen, but narrowed arteries cannot deliver enough blood, causing oxygen starvation known as ischemia. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h1)

question: You notice on your monthly report that many young clients are skipping their second injectable dose. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Stop ordering injectable contraceptives for the clinic entirely
options.B: Organize community education and strengthen client reminder systems
options.C: Refuse care to any client who misses an appointment date
options.D: Wait until the federal ministry sends a special investigation team

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! Spotting a trend like missed doses means we should step up our appointment reminders and patient counseling.

question: What is the primary biological reason for the physical changes women feel during perimenopause?

options.A: Permanent closure of the cervical canal
options.B: Gradual depletion and decreased responsiveness of ovarian follicles
options.C: Complete failure of the anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Sudden permanent stoppage of all thyroid hormones

explanation: As the ovaries naturally run low on active egg follicles, estrogen and progesterone levels start rollercoasting before settling down.

question: Why is medical confidentiality especially critical in occupational health nursing?

options.A: To prevent employers from using private health data to unfairly penalize workers
options.B: To hide mistakes made by the occupational health clinic staff
options.C: To comply with tax laws regarding employee salaries and benefits
options.D: To stop other workers from knowing about common workplace injuries

explanation: Nurses must protect medical information so employees can seek care freely without fear of losing their jobs or facing discrimination. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h2)

question: Long before modern labs, how did early humans figure out which foods were safe to eat?

options.A: Microscopic testing
options.B: Written government guidelines
options.C: Trial and error
options.D: Chemical analysis

explanation: Spot on! Before science labs, our ancestors had to rely on simple observation and trying things out to see what was safe to put in their bodies.

question: A doctor wants to know if a patient's low testosterone is due to a problem in the testes or the pituitary gland. Which test helps figure this out?

options.A: Serum LH and FSH hormone levels
options.B: A prostate-specific antigen blood test
options.C: A complete blood count with differential
options.D: A routine urinalysis and urine culture

explanation: Checking LH and FSH levels from the pituitary gland helps doctors see if the issue starts in the brain (pituitary) or down in the testes. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: A patient has an apical pulse of 110 bpm, but a radial pulse of only 84 bpm. What does this gap mean?

options.A: The automatic blood pressure machine is malfunctioning
options.B: Many heartbeats are not strong enough to create a peripheral pulse wave
options.C: The patient is experiencing a severe drop in body temperature
options.D: The blood pressure cuff was wrapped too tightly around the arm

explanation: This is called a pulse deficit! The heart is beating away (110 times), but some beats are too weak to send a wave all the way down to the wrist. Always check both when you suspect rhythm trouble.

question: What is the main difference between presumptive and probable signs of pregnancy?

options.A: Probable signs only show up right before birth
options.B: Presumptive signs are things the mother feels herself, while probable signs are things a nurse or doctor observes
options.C: Presumptive signs mean the baby is healthy, while probable signs mean trouble
options.D: Presumptive signs need lab tests, while probable signs need X-rays

explanation: Think of presumptive as what the client experiences (like nausea) and probable as what we find during our physical checks as clinicians!

question: Why does the pressure to have a baby boy often weigh so heavily on mothers in patriarchal societies?

options.A: Because society ties a woman's worth and security to producing a son
options.B: Because female children require more expensive healthcare services
options.C: Because local laws fine families that do not have a male child
options.D: Because boys are biologically easier to raise during infancy

explanation: In many traditional setups, a woman's peace of mind and place in the home are unfairly linked to bearing a male heir.

question: Why is getting male partners involved so important for family planning programs in Nigeria?

options.A: Male partners must administer all injectable contraceptives
options.B: Men often hold decision-making power regarding household health and finances
options.C: Hospitals legally prohibit women from buying contraception alone
options.D: Men are the only family members who suffer from reproductive infections

explanation: In many of our communities, men make the major household and financial decisions. If we leave them out of the conversation, family planning programs rarely succeed!

question: What is the main job of a negative feedback loop in the endocrine system?

options.A: To destroy excess neurotransmitters in synapses
options.B: To prevent hormone levels from rising too high
options.C: To amplify initial chemical signals rapidly
options.D: To stimulate continuous runaway glandular growth

explanation: Negative feedback is like a thermostat: when things get high enough, it tells the system to turn down the heat and restore balance.

question: Why do children get medication doses calculated by body weight instead of a standard adult dose?

options.A: Children metabolize all drugs faster than adult patients
options.B: Children have developing organ systems and varying body sizes
options.C: Liquid medications always require weight-based measurements
options.D: Standard adult doses are illegal to give to anyone under age twelve

explanation: Kids aren't just tiny adults! Because their little bodies and metabolic organs are still growing, weight-based dosing keeps them safe from accidental overdoses.

question: Why do clinical training programs for PAC providers include values clarification exercises?

options.A: To help staff recognize and manage personal biases that affect patient care
options.B: To improve the physical cleaning speed of surgical instruments
options.C: To train clinicians on repairing complex abdominal hernias
options.D: To teach nurses how to calculate hospital drug purchase budgets

explanation: As nurses, we learn to separate our personal beliefs from our professional duty, ensuring every patient gets respectful, non-judgmental emergency care.

question: What causes that unpleasant smell in some gas?

options.A: Sulfur compounds produced by specific gut bacteria
options.B: The breakdown of proteins by liver enzymes
options.C: High levels of pure oxygen from swallowed air
options.D: Undigested stomach acid reaching the rectum

explanation: Certain helpful (and smelly!) bacteria release tiny amounts of sulfur when they break down food. Totally normal body process!

question: Why is tracing sexual partners and notifying them so important after an STI diagnosis?

options.A: It punishes individuals who fail to use proper barrier protection
options.B: It proves whether the patient acquired the infection locally
options.C: It breaks the cycle of reinfection and treats exposed individuals
options.D: It provides statistical data for insurance companies to adjust rates

explanation: Exactly! Partner notification ensures everyone gets tested and treated so they don't keep passing the infection back and forth.

question: What is the primary function of the human skin as a body system?

options.A: Regulating core body temperature through voluntary muscle contraction
options.B: Synthesizing primary digestive enzymes for nutrient breakdown
options.C: Acting as a protective barrier against external pathogens
options.D: Producing red blood cells for systemic circulation

explanation: The skin protects underlying structures from environmental threats, injury, and fluid loss. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h1)

question: How do active muscle movements during AROM help with blood circulation?

options.A: They make the arteries much wider and longer permanently.
options.B: They remove all red blood cells from the lower extremities.
options.C: They act as a physical pump pushing blood back toward the heart.
options.D: They completely stop the heart from beating too fast.

explanation: Think of the muscles as a natural pump! As they squeeze, they push blood back up toward the heart against gravity, keeping clots away.

question: Which vitamin is especially important in early pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects in the baby?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Folate
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: You nailed it! Folate (or folic acid) is vital during the early weeks of pregnancy to help the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly.

question: Which of these is a common biological reason for sexual dysfunction in older women?

options.A: Hyperactive thyroid function
options.B: Hormonal shifts during menopause
options.C: Excessive pelvic muscle tone
options.D: Increased production of estrogen

explanation: You've got it! Lower estrogen levels during menopause can cause dryness and tissue changes, which sometimes make things a bit uncomfortable.

question: Why would you pass a nasogastric (NG) tube for a patient dealing with a bowel obstruction?

options.A: Gastric decompression and drainage
options.B: Measuring exact daily urine output
options.C: Continuous monitoring of blood pressure
options.D: Intravenous fluid replacement therapy

explanation: When the bowel is blocked, nothing moves down. An NG tube helps drain out built-up gas and fluid so the patient's stomach feels much relieved! Great job keeping this clinical logic clear.

question: How should an airport security check be handled for a passenger with a pacemaker?

options.A: Turn off the pacemaker completely using an external switch before entering the security line
options.B: Walk through the metal detector normally, but ask security to avoid using a hand-held wand over the chest
options.C: Show the medical card and demand a full body cavity search instead of walking through arches
options.D: Refuse all security screening because airport machines will instantly destroy the pacemaker

explanation: Walking through the security arch is usually fine if you keep moving, but security should avoid holding a magnetic wand directly over the chest. Practical knowledge for clinical practice!

question: What should a nurse do if a visitor enters an isolation room without wearing the required PPE?

options.A: Ignore it if they promise not to touch the patient
options.B: Ask another staff member to handle the situation later
options.C: Report the visitor to hospital security immediately
options.D: Politely stop them, explain the rules, and help them put on PPE

explanation: Educating visitors and ensuring they wear correct gear prevents breaches in the barrier system. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred during reproductive health counselling?

options.A: They shorten the time needed to complete patient registration
options.B: They encourage clients to share their thoughts and concerns fully
options.C: They ensure the nurse makes all the final medical decisions
options.D: They prevent clients from asking complicated medical questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow clients to express their true feelings and personal stories rather than giving a simple one-word answer. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: Why would a doctor order an Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) test for an asphyxiated patient?

options.A: To measure blood acidity and gas levels directly
options.B: To screen the blood stream for infectious bacteria
options.C: To count the exact number of red blood cells
options.D: To check if the patient took any prescription drugs

explanation: An ABG gives a direct look at how much oxygen and carbon dioxide are floating around, plus the blood's pH. Super helpful during respiratory distress!

question: Which of these actions is a serious breach of ethical nursing practice when taking a history?

options.A: Asking a family member to step out while taking a sensitive history
options.B: Discussing a patient's medical history in a public hospital hallway
options.C: Asking clarifying questions about the onset of a headache
options.D: Documenting the patient's social habits in their official chart

explanation: Well done! Talking about patient health details where others can hear breaks patient confidentiality and trust.

question: Why does diabetes mellitus significantly increase a person's risk for developing CAD?

options.A: Pancreatic failure lowers the overall volume of body fluids
options.B: High blood sugar damages blood vessel linings over time
options.C: Extra sugar in the blood thickens the heart valves directly
options.D: Diabetes forces the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells

explanation: Chronic high blood glucose levels injure the delicate inner lining of arteries, making it much easier for plaque to form. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure thirty minutes after giving a blood pressure medication to see if it dropped into the normal range. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Checking the results after an intervention to see if goals were met is the definition of the evaluation phase. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: A patient with persistent asthma is prescribed a daily inhaler that works for 12 hours. What drug class is this?

options.A: Short-acting anticholinergics
options.B: Short-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.C: Long-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.D: Inhaled corticosteroids

explanation: That's a Long-Acting Beta-Agonist (LABA)! While SABAs are for quick rescue, LABAs provide steady, long-lasting control throughout the day.

question: How do peer support groups help survivors of gender-based violence?

options.A: They provide direct financial grants for housing and business start-ups
options.B: They handle all legal investigations and courtroom representations
options.C: They reduce feelings of isolation by connecting survivors with others who share similar experiences
options.D: They replace the need for professional medical checkups and laboratory tests

explanation: Brilliant! Talking with others who truly understand helps survivors realize they are not alone on their healing journey.

question: Which part of the nephron features a dense brush border designed for heavy reabsorption?

options.A: Loop of Henle
options.B: Collecting duct
options.C: Proximal convoluted tubule
options.D: Distal convoluted tubule

explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined with microvilli that form a brush border, maximizing its ability to reabsorb nutrients and water from the filtrate. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why do social and religious pressures in many Nigerian communities often make emotional recovery harder for a PAC patient?

options.A: They force clients to hide their experiences and suffer in silence
options.B: They require mandatory public announcements of medical records
options.C: They prohibit nurses from administering physical pain relief
options.D: They mandate automatic psychiatric admission for every patient

explanation: Heavy stigma creates fear of being blamed, making many women bottle up their trauma instead of seeking help.

question: What is the most important first step a nurse should take before starting a health project in a new community?

options.A: A thorough community assessment
options.B: A legal trial for all community leaders
options.C: A complete structural renovation of local hospitals
options.D: A mandatory relocation of residents

explanation: Correct! You have to understand the people, their leaders, and their needs before you can help them effectively.

question: An older adult has had a nagging cough and hoarseness for three months that won't go away. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to purchase over-the-counter cough syrup
options.B: Advise the patient to return only if they cough up blood
options.C: Report these findings to the clinician for further diagnostic evaluation
options.D: Reassure the patient that common colds often last for several months

explanation: Great clinical thinking! A cough that lasts that long without healing is a classic warning sign that needs a proper doctor's assessment right away.

question: What is the most serious and permanent complication of untreated onchocerciasis?

options.A: Blindness
options.B: Paraplegia
options.C: Deafness
options.D: Kidney failure

explanation: Long-term eye inflammation from dying microfilariae eventually scars the eye tissue, leading to irreversible river blindness if left untreated.

question: What is one of the earliest psychological signs that a patient is entering shock?

options.A: Extreme euphoria
options.B: Deep, heavy snoring
options.C: Sudden memory loss
options.D: Restlessness and anxiety

explanation: As oxygen delivery to the brain decreases, patients often become restless, anxious, or confused before losing consciousness. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why do many young women and teenagers in Nigeria end up turning to unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies over modern medicine
options.B: Easy availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas
options.C: Lack of financial resources and reproductive health access
options.D: Strict enforcement of mandatory hospital reporting laws

explanation: Poverty, fear of social stigma, and struggling to find safe, legal services often push vulnerable girls into dangerous alternatives. As nurses, keeping our clinics open and welcoming is key to changing this.

question: Why does IMNCI use syndromic case management instead of waiting for lab tests?

options.A: Because children cannot tolerate blood draws
options.B: Because laboratory tests are completely unnecessary in pediatrics
options.C: To prevent nurses from having to check vital signs
options.D: To provide fast, life-saving treatment in resource-limited settings

explanation: In busy clinics where labs take time, syndromic management helps nurses spot danger signs and start life-saving treatment right away. You've got this!

question: On a full blood count lab report, what does the abbreviation MCV stand for?

options.A: Minimum capillary vessel
options.B: Measured cellular viscosity
options.C: Mean corpuscular volume
options.D: Maximum clotting velocity

explanation: MCV tells us the average size of the red blood cells. It's super helpful for figuring out what kind of anaemia a patient has!

question: How do barrier methods like condoms actually prevent STIs?

options.A: To permanently neutralize circulating viral loads in the bloodstream
options.B: To increase local mucosal immunity against parasitic invasion
options.C: To block the exchange of infectious bodily fluids during intercourse
options.D: To destroy bacterial cell walls upon contact in the vaginal canal

explanation: You got it! Condoms act as a physical shield so infectious fluids don't pass between partners.

question: Which of these is NOT an automatic (autonomic) body process linked to nerve degeneration?

options.A: Loss of normal bladder control
options.B: Sudden mastery of complex math skills
options.C: Drastic blood pressure drops when standing
options.D: Abnormal sweating patterns

explanation: You definitely don't gain superpowers from nerve degeneration! Autonomic functions control automatic things like blood pressure and sweating.

question: How is a Stage 1 pressure sore best identified on light-skinned patients?

options.A: Intact skin with redness that does not turn white when pressed
options.B: An open crater exposing subcutaneous fat and muscle
options.C: A black, hard scab covering deep tissue damage
options.D: A shallow pink wound with clear fluid drainage

explanation: In Stage 1, the skin isn't broken yet, but it shows redness that stays red even when you press a finger on it (non-blanching). Good to know for your ward rotations! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main use of the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) in the ward?

options.A: To test the patient's long-term memory
options.B: To diagnose the exact cause of a brain injury
options.C: To check the strength of peripheral nerves
options.D: To measure a patient's level of consciousness

explanation: You'll use the GCS every day on clinical placement! It gives us a quick, reliable way to check and record how alert a patient is. You've got this!
